scope: German-language supplemental discovery only. Dispositions compare candidates against the frozen English-list inventory manifests; no system records are created by this file.

candidates.reason: A German article directly identifies SCP as a CP/M-compatible operating system developed by Kombinat Robotron for DDR computers; no matching English-list manifest identity was found.
The German article defines MicroOS/MOS as a FreeDOS-based retro operating system; no matching English-list manifest identity was found. It is distinct from openSUSE MicroOS.
The German article explicitly identifies TCOS as T-Systems' chip-card operating system; no matching English-list manifest identity was found.
The German list calls Amboss a Siemens process-computer operating system, but its target is a red link and no independent identity source was established in this pass.

The German list names COSPAS as a Siemens real-time system used in railway signalling, but it is unlinked; distinguish it from the unrelated COSPAS-SARSAT rescue satellite system before creating an identity.
The German list describes DIPOS for Nixdorf 8862/8864 Banking Network Computers, but its target is a red link; identity, expansion, and relationship to the hardware remain unverified.

Although the German list calls COQOS a real-time OS, the vendor describes the current product as a hypervisor/virtualization SDK that runs guest operating systems; do not catalog it as a standalone OS without a historical-product identity check.

The German list assigns MARTOS to AEG 80-60 process computers and MARTOS-K to AEG 80-20 process computers, but both links are red; verify whether these are separate systems, hardware ports, or releases of one family.
The German list calls RMOS2 and RMOS3 Siemens real-time operating systems but provides no identity links; establish whether the numerals denote releases or distinct system lines.

The German list names BS 3 as an AEG-Telefunken time-sharing OS, but its link resolves to the TR 440 hardware article where it is described as that machine's OS. Preserve the hardware/system boundary pending a dedicated identity decision.
The German list calls BS1000 a historic Siemens batch operating system; it is already represented in English inventory manifest batch-062.
